label: Tweet
summary: A single scene or line, one idea, short enough to read in one breath.

slots.label: Moment
slots.description: The one concrete detail, image, or line worth quoting — a single instant, not a summary of a period or habit.

slots.label: Point
slots.description: The single thought, feeling, or realization the moment stands in for — the reason it's worth saying at all.

research.basis: A tweet's length forces exactly one image and one point — concreteness research says specific detail beats abstraction for engagement, and Graham's essay heuristic says an idea needs both surprise and generality, not more than one of either.
citations: Sadoski, Goetz & Rodriguez 2000 — concreteness was the strongest predictor of interest, comprehensibility, and recall across text types
Graham (paulgraham.com/essay.html) — surprise without generality is gossip, generality without surprise is a textbook; the useful unit is one idea
Green & Brock 2000 — narrative transportation (imagery + affect + attentional focus) drives belief change; splitting attention across more than one point undercuts it
